extracted.intended_audience: regulatory stakeholders (agency staff, employers, labor attorneys), and members of the public searching Federal Register documents about overtime-related rules
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results page listing documents that match the query 'overtime rule', with titles, abstracts, excerpts, links, and metadata across multiple agencies and years. Useful for identifying regulatory standards, notices, proposed and final rules, and related procedural guidance about overtime and related user fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for reduced overtime and holiday inspection fees for small and very small establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: An establishment must meet the thresholds for the small and very small definitions to qualify for reduced overtime and holiday inspection fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSIS will use FSIS Form 5200-16, Overtime/Holiday Rate Reduction Form, to collect information and determine whether an establishment qualifies and the amount of the reduction. Eligible small establishments that apply will receive a 30 percent reduction and eligible very small establishments that apply will receive a 75 percent reduction; establishments must submit FSIS Form 5200-16 for FSIS to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulas and publication requirements for basetime, overtime, and holiday fees (FSIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: FSIS calculates basetime, overtime, and holiday rates using established formulas and publishes annual rates in Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSIS stated it would use formulas to calculate annual rates and publish them; in some cases (e.g., 2026) the Agency may continue to charge prior-year rates if the current-year calculations may not accurately reflect the Agency's cost structure. The notices include tabulated rates and explanation of variables used in the formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job order disclosure requirements regarding overtime for H-2A employers
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, the employer must state in the job order that overtime hours may be available; the wage rate to be paid for any such overtime hours; the circumstances under which overtime hours will be paid; and where the overtime pay is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement appears in regulations implementing H-2A certification and related employer obligations; it clarifies the specific elements an employer must include in the job order with respect to overtime compensation and the conditions for its payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Fair Labor Standards Act to domestic service — companionship and live-in exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The FLSA historically exempted employees who provide companionship services and live-in domestic service employees from minimum wage and overtime requirements; regulatory definitions determine the scope of those exemptions and whether third-party employers may claim them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department has revised these regulations over time (e.g., 1975, 2013 changes narrowing the definition). Proposed rulemaking may restore earlier definitions; the documents discuss anticipated compliance and familiarization costs and consider regulatory alternatives. The discussion frames how definitional changes affect coverage and cost to consumers of services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary-level and duties criteria for white-collar exemptions (executive, administrative, professional, outside sales, computer employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions from minimum wage and overtime for executive, administrative, professional, outside sales, and computer employees depend on duties tests and salary/compensation thresholds (standard salary level and highly compensated employee total annual compensation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed and final rules revise the standard salary level (e.g., raising to particular percentiles of earnings) and the HCE threshold, and add mechanisms to allow timely updating of thresholds (including scheduled initial updates). Discussion includes which employees would gain or lose overtime protections under different salary and duties-test regimes and the methodology for setting levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-fee standards for AMS/FGIS/other agencies — cost-based fees and formula standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: User fees (for grading, inspection, laboratory services, export applications, etc.) must be established based on costs incurred and through standardized formulas that allow agencies to charge reasonable fees sufficient to cover program costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices and rules announce annual rates (regular, overtime, holiday, laboratory services) and explain that cost-based analyses may require rate increases to cover rising operational costs. For FGIS, rulemaking establishes standardized formulas to calculate hourly and unit fees and to re-establish a 3- to 6-month operating reserve as required by statute (United States Grain Standards Act). Agencies publish the rates and the dates the rates will apply (e.g., fiscal/crop year start).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration or technical amendment of exemptions in fee regulations (e.g., AQI commercial aircraft exemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text must correctly reflect exemptions adopted or intended (for example, exemptions for commercial aircraft with 64 or fewer seats); where an editorial error removed an intended exemption, agencies amend regulations to restore it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical amendments restore previously intended exemptions and explain effective dates and any delays; agencies may issue notices requesting information when implementation is delayed and act on comments received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of interpretive rules and policy statements in the CFR — repurposing as sub-regulatory guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of the CFR that are interpretive rules or policy statements which were not issued through notice-and-comment rulemaking should be removed from the CFR and repurposed as sub-regulatory guidance; agencies should solicit comment on which provisions to retain and how to preserve them as guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department distinguishes between legislative rules (force of law) and interpretive rules; it proposes removing from the CFR parts that did not benefit from public comment, with an invitation for stakeholders to comment on retention and guidance formats. This establishes a procedural standard for treating non-legislative statements in the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of rule effective dates for review (Presidential Memorandum practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are to consider postponing for 60 days the effective date of any rule that has not yet taken effect to review questions of fact, law, or policy raised by the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice (cited pursuant to a Presidential Memorandum titled 'Regulatory Freeze Pending Review') has been used to postpone effective dates (e.g., a 60-day postponement of removal of an exemption). Notices explain the legal authority and invite comments during the postponement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying standards for determining joint employer status under labor statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes clarifying how to determine joint employer status under the FLSA and to align determinations under the FMLA and MSPA to the Department's FLSA analysis, providing a nationwide uniform standard for enforcement and greater predictability for employers and workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule marshals commonalities among judicial approaches to simplify enforcement, reduce litigation, and provide a reliable uniform analysis for investigators and stakeholders. The document discusses historical regulatory versions (e.g., 2020 Rule) and the need to reconcile vertical versus horizontal joint employment tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction for calculation of procedural filing and compliance deadlines falling on weekends and Federal holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural regulations may include a rule of construction clarifying how filing and compliance deadlines are calculated when they fall on weekends or Federal holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct final rule clarifies the operation of deadlines to give affected entities greater flexibility in responding to filing deadlines; the change is framed as not adversely affecting operators' ability to provide services and includes statutory/administrative consistency analysis.
